newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight rate rises on short-end tightness.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight rate rises on short-end tightness.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate stayed firm on Monday due to a shortage of funds at the short-end of the market, dealers said.
The overnight traded between 8.0 and 8.5 percent, against Friday's close of 7.5/8.0 percent.
Dealers said short-term interbank rates would remain firm this week because of the squeeze.
"The overnight should stay above eight percent in the next few days as local banks are still short," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
Some dealers have said the squeeze was caused by banks shuffling assets to meet their requirements, including fulfilling statutory reserve requirements.
Earlier, interbank rates were firmer on borrowings by banks and finance companies, dealers said.
They said payments for weekly government treasury bills also firmed rates.
The one-, two- and three-week money were at 7.70/80 percent against 7.50/70 on Friday.
The one-month rate was at 7.60/90 percent from 7.50/60, while three- and six-month money were at 7.50/80 percent against 7.50/60.
Dealers said Bank Negara was believed to have injected funds, through an agent bank, last week to improve market liquidity. No confirmation was available.
Bank Negara's massive intervention to defend the ringgit last month had caused a liquidity squeeze, pushing interbank rates to unusually high levels.
There will be a 500-million ringgit Bank Negara bill issue on Tuesday but this will be matched by a maturity of an issue of a similar amount on Friday, dealers said.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were down across the board, futures dealers said.
At 0900 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) June contract was down six points to 92.42, or an implied yield of 7.58 percent.
September contract fell four to 92.55, or 7.45 percent while December was down three to 92.59, or 7.41 percent.
